newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta staff on hunger strike in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Delta staff on hunger strike in Frankfurt.

text.p: Five Delta Air Lines employees entered the third day of a hunger strike Wednesday to protest large-scale job cuts in Frankfurt, a union official said.
Four men and one woman were camping out in front of Delta check-in counters at Frankfurt airport and refusing food, said Walter Czogalla, the airline's works council chairman.
Conflict between the airline and staff was escalating as Delta pressed ahead with plans to cut staff from 850 down to 250 in Frankfurt and drop eight of its 14 daily flights, he said.
Delta announced in January that it would drop unviable flights from Frankfurt to six European cities and three U.S. destinations by the end of June, with up to 600 job losses.
Czogalla said that walkouts by staff this week, including a protest by several hundred employees on Tuesday, had delayed flights by up to two and a half hours and affected 2,200 passengers.

The works council wants job guarantees for the 250 remaining staff and wants Delta to invest 180 million marks ($107 million), or its expected financial improvement from the restructuring measures, in a social plan that would be valid until 2003, Czogalla said.

Delta's Germany sales manager, Roland Weil, told Reuters the airline was ready to talk with the works council. But he added: "The works council is demanding almost 250,000 marks ($148,280) per employee and that is not acceptable."
No passengers have been left stranded during the walkouts and the delays have been for "acceptable" lengths of time, he said.
